passages.text: Then the LORD appeared to Abraham by the Oaks of Mamre in the heat of the day, while he was sitting at the entrance of his tent.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was sitting at the entrance of his tent.
The day was very hot.
The tent was near the Oaks of Mamre.
The LORD appeared to Abraham.
passages.original: וַיֵּרָ֤א אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה בְּאֵלֹנֵ֖י מַמְרֵ֑א וְה֛וּא יֹשֵׁ֥ב פֶּֽתַח־ הָאֹ֖הֶל כְּחֹ֥ם הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: And Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he ran from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was sitting at the entrance of his tent.
He looked up.
He saw three men standing near him.
Abraham saw them.
He ran from the entrance of his tent to meet them.
He bowed down to the ground before them.
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים נִצָּבִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיַּ֗רְא וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתָם֙ מִפֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֔הֶל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָֽרְצָה׃

passages.text: “My lord,” said Abraham, “if I have found favor in your sight, please do not pass your servant by.
passages.sermon:
Abraham saw three men standing near him.
Abraham ran to meet them.
Abraham bowed low to the ground.
Abraham spoke to them.
Abraham said, “My lord, if I have found favor in your sight, do not pass by your servant.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנָ֗י אִם־ נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ אַל־ נָ֥א תַעֲבֹ֖ר מֵעַ֥ל עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Let a little water be brought, that you may wash your feet and rest yourselves under the tree.
passages.sermon:
Abraham saw three men standing near him.
Abraham wanted to show them kindness.
Abraham said, “Let someone bring a little water.”
“You can wash your feet.”
“You can rest under the tree.”
passages.original: יֻקַּֽח־ נָ֣א מְעַט־ מַ֔יִם וְרַחֲצ֖וּ רַגְלֵיכֶ֑ם וְהִֽשָּׁעֲנ֖וּ תַּ֥חַת הָעֵֽץ׃

passages.text: And I will bring a bit of bread so that you may refresh yourselves. This is why you have passed your servant’s way. After that, you may continue on your way.” “Yes,” they replied, “you may do as you have said.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham spoke to the visitors.
He said, "I will bring a piece of bread."
You can eat and feel refreshed.
You have come this way to visit your servant.
After you eat, you may continue on your journey."
The visitors answered Abraham.
They said, "Yes."
They said, "Do as you have said."
passages.original: וְאֶקְחָ֨ה פַת־ לֶ֜חֶם וְסַעֲד֤וּ לִבְּכֶם֙ אַחַ֣ר תַּעֲבֹ֔רוּ כִּֽי־ עַל־ כֵּ֥ן עֲבַרְתֶּ֖ם עַֽל־ עַבְדְּכֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כֵּ֥ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּֽרְתָּ׃

passages.text: So Abraham hurried into the tent and said to Sarah, “Quick! Prepare three seahs of fine flour, knead it, and bake some bread.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a faithful servant of God.
Abraham saw three visitors near his tent.
Abraham wanted to show them hospitality.
Abraham hurried into the tent.
Sarah was Abraham’s wife.
Abraham spoke to Sarah.
He said, “Quick! Take three seahs of fine flour.
Knead the flour.
Bake some bread.”
passages.original: וַיְמַהֵ֧ר אַבְרָהָ֛ם הָאֹ֖הֱלָה אֶל־ שָׂרָ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מַהֲרִ֞י שְׁלֹ֤שׁ סְאִים֙ קֶ֣מַח סֹ֔לֶת ל֖וּשִׁי וַעֲשִׂ֥י עֻגֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Meanwhile, Abraham ran to the herd, selected a tender and choice calf, and gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a faithful servant of God.
Abraham saw three visitors near his tent.
Abraham wanted to show them hospitality.
Abraham ran to his herd of cattle.
He chose a young calf.
The calf was tender and good.
Abraham gave the calf to a servant.
The servant quickly prepared the calf for the guests.
passages.original: וְאֶל־ הַבָּקָ֖ר רָ֣ץ אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיִּקַּ֨ח בֶּן־ בָּקָ֜ר רַ֤ךְ וָטוֹב֙ וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֶל־ הַנַּ֔עַר וַיְמַהֵ֖ר לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then Abraham brought curds and milk and the calf that had been prepared, and he set them before the men and stood by them under the tree as they ate.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a faithful servant of God.
Abraham took curds and milk.
He also took the calf that he had prepared.
Abraham placed the food in front of the men.
Abraham stood near the men.
He stood under the tree.
The men ate the food.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חֶמְאָ֜ה וְחָלָ֗ב וּבֶן־ הַבָּקָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהֽוּא־ עֹמֵ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם תַּ֥חַת הָעֵ֖ץ וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃

passages.text: “Where is your wife Sarah?” they asked. “There, in the tent,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
Three men visited Abraham.
\r\nThey asked Abraham a question.
\r\nThey said, “Where is your wife Sarah?”
\r\nAbraham answered them.
\r\nHe said, “She is in the tent.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵׄלָׄ֔יׄוׄ אַיֵּ֖ה שָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתֶּ֑ךָ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֵּ֥ה בָאֹֽהֶל׃

passages.text: Then the LORD said, “I will surely return to you at this time next year, and your wife Sarah will have a son!” Now Sarah was behind him, listening at the entrance to the tent.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Abraham.
The LORD said, “I will return to you next year at this time.
Your wife Sarah will have a son.”
Sarah stood behind the LORD.
Sarah listened at the entrance to the tent.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר שׁ֣וֹב אָשׁ֤וּב אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה וְהִנֵּה־ בֵ֖ן לְשָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתֶּ֑ךָ וְשָׂרָ֥ה שֹׁמַ֛עַת פֶּ֥תַח הָאֹ֖הֶל וְה֥וּא אַחֲרָֽיו׃

passages.text: And Abraham and Sarah were already old and well along in years; Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.
passages.sermon:
Abraham was old.
Sarah was old.
They had lived many years.
Sarah could no longer have children.
Sarah had passed the age when women bear children.
passages.original: וְאַבְרָהָ֤ם וְשָׂרָה֙ זְקֵנִ֔ים בָּאִ֖ים בַּיָּמִ֑ים חָדַל֙ לִהְי֣וֹת לְשָׂרָ֔ה אֹ֖רַח כַּנָּשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: So she laughed to herself, saying, “After I am worn out and my master is old, will I now have this pleasure?”
passages.sermon:
Sarah was Abraham’s wife.
Sarah was very old.
Sarah could no longer have children.
Sarah heard the LORD’s promise.
Sarah laughed quietly to herself.
Sarah thought, “I am worn out.”
Sarah thought, “My husband is old.”
Sarah asked herself, “Will I now have this joy?”
passages.original: וַתִּצְחַ֥ק שָׂרָ֖ה בְּקִרְבָּ֣הּ לֵאמֹ֑ר אַחֲרֵ֤י בְלֹתִי֙ הָֽיְתָה־ לִּ֣י עֶדְנָ֔ה וַֽאדֹנִ֖י זָקֵֽן׃

passages.text: And the LORD asked Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh and say, ‘Can I really bear a child when I am old?’
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Abraham.
The LORD asked Abraham a question.
Sarah was Abraham’s wife.
Sarah was old.
Sarah had passed the age of childbearing.
The LORD said, “Why did Sarah laugh?”
The LORD said, “Why did Sarah say, ‘Can I really bear a child when I am old?’”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ אַבְרָהָ֑ם לָ֣מָּה זֶּה֩ צָחֲקָ֨ה שָׂרָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר הַאַ֥ף אֻמְנָ֛ם אֵלֵ֖ד וַאֲנִ֥י זָקַֽנְתִּי׃

passages.text: Is anything too difficult for the LORD? At the appointed time I will return to you—in about a year—and Sarah will have a son.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Abraham.
The LORD has all power.
Nothing is too hard for the LORD.
The LORD said, “At the set time I will return to you.
This will be about a year from now.
Sarah will have a son.”
passages.original: הֲיִפָּלֵ֥א מֵיְהוָ֖ה דָּבָ֑ר לַמּוֹעֵ֞ד אָשׁ֥וּב אֵלֶ֛יךָ כָּעֵ֥ת חַיָּ֖ה וּלְשָׂרָ֥ה בֵֽן׃

passages.text: But Sarah was afraid, so she denied it and said, “I did not laugh.” “No,” replied the LORD, “but you did laugh.”
passages.sermon:
Sarah was afraid.
Sarah denied laughing.
Sarah said, “I did not laugh.”
The LORD replied to Sarah.
The LORD said, “No, you did laugh.”
passages.original: וַתְּכַחֵ֨שׁ שָׂרָ֧ה׀ לֵאמֹ֛ר לֹ֥א צָחַ֖קְתִּי כִּ֣י׀ יָרֵ֑אָה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר׀ לֹ֖א כִּ֥י צָחָֽקְתְּ׃

passages.text: When the men got up to leave, they looked out over Sodom, and Abraham walked along with them to see them off.
passages.sermon:
Three men visited Abraham.
The men got up to leave.
They looked out over Sodom.
Abraham walked with the men.
He went with them to see them off.
passages.original: וַיָּקֻ֤מוּ מִשָּׁם֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיַּשְׁקִ֖פוּ עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם וְאַ֨בְרָהָ֔ם הֹלֵ֥ךְ עִמָּ֖ם לְשַׁלְּחָֽם׃

passages.text: And the LORD said, “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke.
The LORD is God.
The LORD said, “Should I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?”
Abraham is the man God chose.
God considered whether to tell Abraham His plans.
passages.original: וַֽיהֹוָ֖ה אָמָ֑ר הַֽמְכַסֶּ֤ה אֲנִי֙ מֵֽאַבְרָהָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: Abraham will surely become a great and powerful nation, and through him all the nations of the earth will be blessed.
passages.sermon:
Abraham is a man chosen by God.
God will make Abraham into a great nation.
This nation will be powerful.
All the nations of the earth will receive blessing through Abraham.
passages.original: וְאַ֨בְרָהָ֔ם הָי֧וֹ יִֽהְיֶ֛ה לְג֥וֹי גָּד֖וֹל וְעָצ֑וּם וְנִ֨בְרְכוּ ב֔וֹ כֹּ֖ל גּוֹיֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: For I have chosen him, so that he will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just, in order that the LORD may bring upon Abraham what He has promised.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD chose Abraham.
The LORD wanted Abraham to command his children.
The LORD wanted Abraham to command his household after him.
Abraham must teach them to keep the way of the LORD.
They must do what is right.
They must do what is just.
The LORD will do this so He can bring on Abraham what He promised.
The LORD will fulfill His word to Abraham.
passages.original: כִּ֣י יְדַעְתִּ֗יו לְמַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְצַוֶּ֜ה אֶת־ בָּנָ֤יו וְאֶת־ בֵּיתוֹ֙ אַחֲרָ֔יו וְשָֽׁמְרוּ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יְהוָ֔ה לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת צְדָקָ֖ה וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט לְמַ֗עַן הָבִ֤יא יְהוָה֙ עַל־ אַבְרָהָ֔ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֖ר עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then the LORD said, “The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great. Because their sin is so grievous, I will go down to see if their actions fully justify the outcry that has reached Me. If not, I will find out.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke.
The LORD said the outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great.
Their sin is very serious.
I will go down now.
I will see if their actions match the outcry that has come to Me.
If they have done all this evil, I will know.
If not, I will find out.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה זַעֲקַ֛ת סְדֹ֥ם וַעֲמֹרָ֖ה כִּי־ רָ֑בָּה וְחַ֨טָּאתָ֔ם כִּ֥י כָבְדָ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃ אֵֽרֲדָה־ נָּ֣א וְאֶרְאֶ֔ה הַכְּצַעֲקָתָ֛הּ הַבָּ֥אָה אֵלַ֖י עָשׂ֣וּ׀ כָּלָ֑ה וְאִם־ לֹ֖א אֵדָֽעָה׃

passages.text: And the two men turned away and went toward Sodom, but Abraham remained standing before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Two men stood with Abraham and the LORD.
The two men turned away from that place.
The two men went toward Sodom.
Abraham did not leave.
Abraham remained standing before the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּפְנ֤וּ מִשָּׁם֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ סְדֹ֑מָה וְאַ֨בְרָהָ֔ם עוֹדֶ֥נּוּ עֹמֵ֖ד לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Abraham stepped forward and said, “Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a faithful servant of God.
Abraham stepped forward.
Abraham spoke to the LORD.
Abraham asked a question.
Abraham said, “Will You destroy the righteous together with the wicked?”
passages.original: וַיִּגַּ֥שׁ אַבְרָהָ֖ם וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַאַ֣ף תִּסְפֶּ֔ה צַדִּ֖יק עִם־ רָשָֽׁע׃

passages.text: What if there are fifty righteous ones in the city? Will You really sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous ones who are there?
passages.sermon:
Abraham spoke to the LORD.
Abraham asked about the city of Sodom.
He said, "What if there are fifty righteous people in the city?"
He asked, "Will You really destroy the city?"
He asked, "Will You not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous people who are there?"
passages.original: אוּלַ֥י יֵ֛שׁ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים צַדִּיקִ֖ם בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעִ֑יר הַאַ֤ף תִּסְפֶּה֙ וְלֹא־ תִשָּׂ֣א לַמָּק֔וֹם לְמַ֛עַן חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים הַצַּדִּיקִ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּקִרְבָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: Far be it from You to do such a thing—to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous and the wicked are treated alike. Far be it from You! Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?”
passages.sermon:
Abraham spoke to the LORD.
Abraham said, "You are the Judge of all the earth.
You must do what is right.
You must not kill righteous people together with wicked people.
You must not treat righteous people the same as wicked people.
You must not do such a thing."
passages.original: חָלִ֨לָה לְּךָ֜ מֵעֲשֹׂ֣ת׀ כַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה לְהָמִ֤ית צַדִּיק֙ עִם־ רָשָׁ֔ע וְהָיָ֥ה כַצַּדִּ֖יק כָּרָשָׁ֑ע חָלִ֣לָה לָּ֔ךְ הֲשֹׁפֵט֙ כָּל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ לֹ֥א יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: So the LORD replied, “If I find fifty righteous ones within the city of Sodom, on their account I will spare the whole place.”
passages.sermon: The LORD spoke.\r\nThe LORD is the Judge of all the earth.\r\nThe LORD said, "If I find fifty righteous people in Sodom, I will spare the whole city for their sake."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה אִם־ אֶמְצָ֥א בִסְדֹ֛ם חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים צַדִּיקִ֖ם בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעִ֑יר וְנָשָׂ֥אתִי לְכָל־ הַמָּק֖וֹם בַּעֲבוּרָֽם׃

passages.text: Then Abraham answered, “Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord—though I am but dust and ashes— suppose the fifty righteous ones lack five. Will You destroy the whole city for the lack of five?” He replied, “If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy it.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham spoke to the Lord.
Abraham said, “I have dared to speak to you, Lord.
I am only dust and ashes.
Suppose there are fifty righteous people, but five are missing.
Will you destroy the whole city because of those five?
The Lord answered Abraham.
The Lord said, “If I find forty-five righteous people there, I will not destroy the city.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן אַבְרָהָ֖ם וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הִנֵּה־ נָ֤א הוֹאַ֙לְתִּי֙ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־ אֲדֹנָ֔י וְאָנֹכִ֖י עָפָ֥ר וָאֵֽפֶר׃ א֠וּלַי יַחְסְר֞וּן חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים הַצַּדִּיקִם֙ חֲמִשָּׁ֔ה הֲתַשְׁחִ֥ית בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אֶת־ כָּל־ הָעִ֑יר וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אַשְׁחִ֔ית אִם־ אֶמְצָ֣א שָׁ֔ם אַרְבָּעִ֖ים וַחֲמִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: Once again Abraham spoke to the LORD, “Suppose forty are found there?” He answered, “On account of the forty, I will not do it.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham was a faithful servant of God.
Abraham spoke to the LORD again.
Abraham said, "Suppose forty righteous people are found there."
The LORD answered Abraham.
The LORD said, "I will not destroy the city because of the forty righteous people."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨סֶף ע֜וֹד לְדַבֵּ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אוּלַ֛י יִמָּצְא֥וּן שָׁ֖ם אַרְבָּעִ֑ים וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֔ה בַּעֲב֖וּר הָאַרְבָּעִֽים׃

passages.text: Then Abraham said, “May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak further. Suppose thirty are found there?” He replied, “If I find thirty there, I will not do it.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham spoke to the Lord.
Abraham said, "Please do not be angry with me.
Let me speak again.
Suppose there are thirty righteous people in the city.
Will you destroy the city if there are thirty righteous people?"
The Lord answered Abraham.
The Lord said, "If I find thirty righteous people there, I will not destroy the city."
passages.original: וַ֠יֹּאמֶר אַל־ נָ֞א יִ֤חַר לַֽאדֹנָי֙ וַאֲדַבֵּ֔רָה אוּלַ֛י יִמָּצְא֥וּן שָׁ֖ם שְׁלֹשִׁ֑ים וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֔ה אִם־ אֶמְצָ֥א שָׁ֖ם שְׁלֹשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: And Abraham said, “Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord, suppose twenty are found there?” He answered, “On account of the twenty, I will not destroy it.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham spoke to the Lord.
Abraham had already asked the Lord several times about sparing the city.
Abraham said, “I have dared to speak to the Lord.”
Abraham said, “Suppose twenty righteous people are found there?”
The Lord answered Abraham.
The Lord said, “I will not destroy the city because of the twenty.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּֽה־ נָ֤א הוֹאַ֙לְתִּי֙ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־ אֲדֹנָ֔י אוּלַ֛י יִמָּצְא֥וּן שָׁ֖ם עֶשְׂרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אַשְׁחִ֔ית בַּעֲב֖וּר הָֽעֶשְׂרִֽים׃

passages.text: Finally, Abraham said, “May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak once more. Suppose ten are found there?” And He answered, “On account of the ten, I will not destroy it.”
passages.sermon:
Abraham spoke to the Lord.
Abraham said, “Please do not be angry with me.”
Abraham asked to speak one more time.
Abraham said, “Suppose ten people are found there?”
The Lord answered Abraham.
The Lord said, “I will not destroy the city if I find ten people there.”
passages.original: וַ֠יֹּאמֶר אַל־ נָ֞א יִ֤חַר לַֽאדֹנָי֙ וַאֲדַבְּרָ֣ה אַךְ־ הַפַּ֔עַם אוּלַ֛י יִמָּצְא֥וּן שָׁ֖ם עֲשָׂרָ֑ה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א אַשְׁחִ֔ית בַּעֲב֖וּר הָעֲשָׂרָֽה׃

passages.text: When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, He departed, and Abraham returned home.
passages.sermon: The LORD finished speaking with Abraham.\r\nThe LORD left.\r\nAbraham returned to his home.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר כִּלָּ֔ה לְדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל־ אַבְרָהָ֑ם וְאַבְרָהָ֖ם שָׁ֥ב לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃
